clearedSpotChecks.check: The two lookup tables the JUMPI path reads from the shipped ELF's data: CSWTCH.2401 at 0x810800 (negate_comparison) and the switch table of Emitter::conditional_jmp at 0x8107c0, decoded to the asmjit instruction id of each arm.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I read the disassembly of conditional_jmp at 0x36f430 in research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/dl/dis/monad-0.16.7.s myself. It bounds the Comparison at 9 (cmp edx,0x9; ja ret), indexes the table at 0x8107c0 and each arm passes one id to BaseEmitter::_emitI: 0x13e, 0x14a, 0x13b, 0x13a, 0x139, 0x13c, 0x142, 0x141, 0x140, 0x143. I could not fetch the asmjit id enum (raw.githubusercontent.com/asmjit/asmjit returned 404 for x86globals.h on master, main and v1.14), so I checked the ids against the binary instead: they fit an alphabetical enum with ja 0x139, jae 0x13a, jb 0x13b, jbe 0x13c, je 0x13e, jg 0x140, jge 0x141, jl 0x142, jle 0x143, jmp 0x144, jnb 0x147, jne 0x14a, jnz 0x152. jump_non_literal_dest at 0x391d30 emits 0x147 after a cmp and 0x144 for the final jump, which is jnb for the range check and jmp for the jump. The source table at virtual_stack.hpp:100-127 (cycle 31 download) maps each code to its negation, as the unit says. The 'raw' values in out/cctables.json are each code's negation index. I did not reread the four bytes at 0x810800 from the ELF myself. I read them through cctables.py and its output.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 1 and Task 2 at the terminator: all 128 terminators equal the clang listing, and 256,000 runs plus 22,400 synthetic runs choose the same successor as pyevm.py, including jumps through the jump table with destinations that have bits 64, 128, 192 or 255 set.
clearedSpotChecks.note: out/term.json reports runs 256000, badRuns 0, flagged 0, stops 0, seed 3333. The jump-table path matters most here, because a destination whose high limbs are ignored could land on a valid JUMPDEST. I read jump_non_literal_dest at 0x391d30 in the disassembly. It emits a cmp then jnb (0x147) to the error label for the low limb against the bytecode size, then two ORs (0x1eb) of the upper limbs and jnz (0x152) to the error label, then the indexed load, add and jmp (0x144). All four limbs are checked, so a word above 2^64 cannot reach the table. The fault runs in term-faults.log show that the harness catches an inverted code and a condition test that skips limbs. One caveat stands: two terminators depend on a limb order taken from the clang listing, as the unit records. That does not open a path, because the PoolManager's jump destinations are pushed by its own code and are not values a caller supplies.

clearedSpotChecks.note: On 2026-11-27 I ran my own read-only calls to https://rpc.monad.xyz. web3_clientVersion returned Monad/0.16.7. The first eth_getCode returned 'Rate limit exceeded'. The retry returned 24,009 bytes with sha256 prefix 288b97729c9e4f34, which equals networks.json and the unit. I read src/libraries/FullMath.sol:21-26 (mulmod with not(0), prod1 by sub and lt), :30 require(denominator > prod1), :33-37 div when prod1 == 0, :46-99 remainder, twos and the Newton inverse, and :111-114 the rounding increment with require(++result > 0). They match the unit's description. With the branches at :30, :33 and :112 emitted as the EVM takes them, I found no change to mulDiv's results.
